mac_setup_notes:
Source pages: $HOME/projects/libredb/libredb-studio/docs/llms/README.md, methodology.md, setup.md, model-tuning.md, bonsai/bonsai-2.md, liquid/lfm3.md, ornith/ornith.md, muse/muse-glimmer.md. Facts that matter for transfer (all measured on the M5 Max, libredb-studio):
- Hardware: Apple M5 Max, 64 GB unified memory, macOS high-power mode on AC (methodology.md "The machine"). Apple's spec page lists 64 GB only for the M5 Max with the 40-core GPU, at 614 GB/s (https://www.apple.com/macbook-pro/specs/). This laptop's GPU has 896 GB/s, 1.46x that, but only 15.47 GiB of CUDA memory. Methodology says high-power mode alone was worth 2.8x throughput, and a long sweep lost cells to thermals, so lost cells were re-measured on a rested machine. The timings are best-case runs on a rested machine.
- Engine versions are not uniform across this lane. The general method was Ollama 0.32.13 and 0.33.0 (22-23 Aug 2026), and gemma4:12b went from 5/5 to 1/5 between those two engine versions. bonsai-2 was measured 17-22 Oct 2026 on Ollama 0.40.6 across four app builds, and its 2b row depends on a server-side blank-locator fix (bonsai-2.md "Where these figures are softest"). lfm3 was measured on Ollama 0.40.13 because it refuses older versions (lfm3.md). The ornith and muse pages name no engine, so they presumably used 0.32.13/0.33.0.
- Transport: Ollama's OpenAI-compatible /v1 endpoint, with temperature 0 and topP 1 by default (model-tuning.md). That overrides the Ollama Modelfile sampling (bonsai temp 1 + presence_penalty 1, ornith temp 0.6, muse temp 1). OpenCode will not send temperature 0 unless configured to.
- Context: the lane pages set no context bound. Six other models needed OLLAMA_CONTEXT_LENGTH=32768 (qwen3.6.md:68-69), so these ran at whatever Ollama defaults to on a 64 GB Mac. That is not stated, and it is not the 4k default this <24 GiB GPU gets.
- Thinking: libredb can suppress reasoning per model through suppressPlanReasoning and suppressAgentReasoning. ornith:35b passed only with both on. muse-glimmer passed only with plan reasoning off. bonsai-2:9b passed only with agent reasoning off. bonsai-2:2b and 4b needed temperature 0.3 and verdict/compare hold limits of 5. ornith:9b needed one extra plan turn. lfm3 needed no settings. muse-glimmer also needed a 150 s turn limit and reportReminderLimit 2.
- Per-turn limit: 90 s shipped. Of this lane, only muse-glimmer carries 150 s.
- Pass bar: six surfaces x five consecutive passes against an SQLite sample. Answer correctness is "largely unchecked" (methodology.md "What is not covered").
- Durations are whole agent runs (prefill + decode + tool turns), not tok/s. The methodology itself says to treat pass/fail as the transferable part and the seconds as a lower bound on smaller machines.
- Disk sizes on the Mac match the Linux GGUF tags for bonsai, ornith and muse. They do not match for lfm3:1.7b: the Mac shows 1.7 GB, while the Linux GGUF Q4_K_M is 1.1 GB and the tag page shows "1.1GB - 1.7GB". So the Mac very likely ran a different (MLX) artifact (inference).

models.fit_detail: (estimate) Weights 0.51 GiB, projector 0.34 GiB. KV is 12 KiB/token in f16 (6 full-attention layers x 2 KV heads x 256, per Qwen3.5-2B config.json): 0.75 GiB at 64k, 3 GiB at 256K. GDN state and compute buffers add about 0.5-1 GiB. The total is about 2-3 GiB at 64k, far under 15.47 GiB. No system RAM needed beyond the process.
models.best_runtime_here: Ollama (bonsai-2:2b, same file and parser that were tested), with OLLAMA_CONTEXT_LENGTH=65536 and a pinned version of at least 0.40.6. llama.cpp b12407 also runs Q2_0 per the KB, but the tool parser path differs from the one tested.
models.speed_here_vs_mac: (estimate) Similar or faster. The model fits fully, so decode is bandwidth-bound or overhead-bound and this GPU has 1.46x the Mac's 614 GB/s. Run time is dominated by the model's re-reading behaviour, though, not by tok/s. Q2_0 CUDA kernel speed under Ollama is unmeasured.
models.reason: It fits trivially, but it is the least stable passer on the roster (14 s to 5:24) and needed tuning plus a server fix. As a 2B ternary model it brings nothing to an OpenCode coding workflow. At most it is a stack smoke test.

models.best_runtime_here: Ollama ornith:9b with OLLAMA_CONTEXT_LENGTH=65536 (or 131072), OLLAMA_FLASH_ATTENTION=1, one parallel slot. models.speed_here_vs_mac: (estimate) Faster. It sits fully in VRAM, and the decode ceiling is about 159 vs 109 tok/s (5.63 GB read per token at 896 vs 614 GB/s), about 1.46x. Prefill on the RTX 5080 is likely no slower. The Mac's 31 s median is whole-run time, so expect the same order or a little less, not a straight 1.46x.
models.reason: It is the only model in this lane that combines a full fit with headroom for 128k, a clean first-hand 30/30 tool-loop record with almost no tuning, a 31 s median, and a coding-agent post-training target. The KB's exclusion was aimed at Ornith-1.5 and its vLLM NVFP4 path, not at this Ollama GGUF. The provenance concern (unverified org) remains and should be stated.

models.fit_detail: (estimate) Weights 19.71 GiB exceed 15.47 GiB. KV is 20 KiB/token f16 (10 full-attention layers x 2 KV x 256): 1.25 GiB at 64k, 2.5 GiB at 128k. With Ollama's whole-layer split (about 0.49 GiB per layer) roughly 24-26 of 40 layers fit on the GPU and about 7-8 GiB go to RAM. With llama.cpp the same architecture as the KB's Qwen3.6-35B-A3B recipe applies: --n-cpu-moe about 21 at 128k (about 8.9 GiB of experts in RAM) or about 18-19 at 64k. RAM need is about 8-9 GiB plus the process, well inside the 40 GiB free.
models.best_runtime_here: llama.cpp b12407 with ornith-ai/Ornith-1.0-35B-GGUF Q4_K_M, -ngl all --n-cpu-moe ~21 -c 65536 or 131072 -fa on --jinja, thinking off, following the Qwen3.6-35B-A3B recipe in llamacpp/models.md. That beats Ollama's layer split for a MoE. Caveat: llama.cpp's handling of Ornith's tool format is untested, while Ollama's 'ornith' parser is what passed the harness.
models.speed_here_vs_mac: (estimate) Slower. The Mac holds all 19.7 GiB in 614 GB/s memory. Here the routed experts of about half the layers are read from DDR5 (about 102 GB/s peak) on every token, so decode drops to roughly the KB's Qwen3.6-35B-A3B offload range rather than scaling up. Mac run times (median 36 s, investigate 1:37) should be read as a lower bound here.
models.reason: The harness itself shows it is slower than ornith:9b and passes only with thinking fully suppressed. On this laptop it spills to RAM. The same MoE slot is already covered by KB rank 2, Qwen3.6-35B-A3B, which has the same architecture, the same recipe and stronger independent evidence.

models.opencode_suitability: Tools, thinking and vision, 128K context (enough for 64k). The libredb evidence shows reliable tool use (a passing assess calls 11 tools), but only with plan thinking off, a 150 s turn limit and an extra report reminder. In other words it works, but slowly, and sometimes stops without filing.
models.fit_detail: (estimate) Ollama Q4_K_M weights are 15.61 GiB plus a 1.30 GiB projector, already over 15.47 GiB. KV is small: 13 KiB/token f16 for the 13 global layers, about 0.8 GiB at 64k, plus about 80 MiB of SWA. Ollama would place roughly 38-42 of 52 dense layers on the GPU and about 3.5-4.5 GiB in RAM. All-in-VRAM is possible only with a smaller llama.cpp quant, for example unsloth UD-Q3_K_XL at 12.44 GiB or UD-IQ3_XXS at 12.23 GiB, text-only, about 14.5-15 GiB at 64k. That is tight, and it is a different quant from the one that passed.
models.best_runtime_here: If tried at all: llama.cpp b12407 (it has LLM_ARCH_MUSE_GLIMMER) with unsloth/Muse-Glimmer-30B-GGUF UD-Q3_K_XL, -ngl all, -c 65536, no mmproj, thinking off. That fits fully, which Ollama's Q4_K_M cannot. Ollama with the tested Q4_K_M would spill dense layers to DDR5.
models.speed_here_vs_mac: (estimate) Slower with the tested Q4_K_M on Ollama. A dense model reads every weight per token, and about 25% of them would come from DDR5 at about 102 GB/s peak against the Mac's 614 GB/s for all of them. That is roughly half the Mac's decode rate, so the 115 s median and 150 s per-turn limit would likely be exceeded. With UD-Q3_K_XL fully in VRAM, decode could be similar to or faster than the Mac, but at a lower quant whose agent reliability is unmeasured.
models.reason: It is the slowest passer even on the Mac, needs three harness-specific crutches, and either spills (tested quant) or runs at an untested Q3 quant here. The KB's exclusion holds. This evidence adds a confirmed tool-reliability note but no reason to rank it.

kb_implications: Disambiguate Ornith in docs/model-selection.md:300 and vllm/models.md:690. The KB's exclusion is about Ornith-1.5-9B (Ollama repo ornith-1.5, vision, 6.6 GB). The user's harness passed Ornith-1.0-9B (Ollama repo ornith, tag ornith:9b, text-only, Q4_K_M 5.24 GiB, parser 'ornith') 30/30 with only one extra plan turn, a 31 s median and a 1:58 slowest run (measured on the M5 Max, libredb-studio). Add Ornith-1.0-9B as an honorable mention or trial for an Ollama all-in-VRAM agent at 64k-128k (about 8.5-10.5 GiB, estimate). Keep the unverified-org caveat, but note that first-hand tool-loop reliability now exists for the 1.0 GGUF on Ollama, and that the vLLM NVFP4 crash reason does not apply to this path.
